subject: Trial environment bridge: org bootstrap, API keying, IP allowlist & VPC peering schedule
messages:
From: Sam Holland <sam.holland@medsync.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Trial run — environment & timeline questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. We're excited to run the trial but need to lock down a short mutual plan so our IT and procurement teams can align — specifically: API key provisioning, org bootstrap (tenant + roles), IP allowlist entries, and VPC peering options.

Can you confirm the minimum artifacts your team needs from us to open the trial environment? We're aiming for a 2-week evaluation window starting the week of Aug 24, but procurement has asked for a clear close timeline and a checklist they can sign off on.

I've attached a draft MAP (MedSync_MAP_v1.xlsx) with internal milestones; procurement copied this email (procurement@medsync.com).

High-level asks from our side:
- Fast path to an API key or ephemeral credential for dev testing
- Steps to create our org and one sandbox tenant (roles, permissions)
- IP allowlist entries and recommended CIDR ranges for peering
- If peering is required, whether Redwood supports transit VPC or only direct peering

If you can send a short runbook or a checklist we can circulate internally, that would help speed approvals.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Holland
Director, Integrations
MedSync Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Trial run — environment & timeline questions

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list and the draft MAP.

We can absolutely support a compact, 2-week evaluation. Proposed minimal MAP steps (we'll own the Redwood-side actions in parentheses):
1) Org bootstrap: we create the trial tenant and invite your admin account (Neha: create tenant + send org invite).
2) API keys: we can issue an ephemeral API key for dev testing within 24 hours of tenant creation; production-grade keys follow after org verification (Ben: pricing/limits noted).
3) IP allowlist: provide the public IP ranges your testers will use. We accept single IPs or CIDR blocks; for peering we need non-overlapping private CIDRs.
4) VPC peering: supported for AWS (Direct VPC peering) and GCP VPC peering; transit VPC is possible with the networking team but will add time. CS (Marissa) will propose the peering playbook and calendar.

Immediate asks for your IT/procurement to unblock the trial:
- AWS account ID (or GCP project number) for peering
- CIDR ranges you plan to use (non-overlapping 10.0.0.0/8 subset recommended)
- Contact for network engineering (email + preferred meeting window)
- PO/Procurement contact if a commercial order or credit memo is needed to start dedicated capacity trials

Proposed timeline (if we start org bootstrap on Aug 24):
- Aug 24: tenant creation + org invite
- Aug 25: ephemeral API key issued; smoke tests run by MedSync
- Aug 26-27: IP allowlist confirmed; peering request submitted if required
- Aug 31: optional peering window (if MedSync chooses peering)
- Sep 7: end of 2-week evaluation; check-in and success criteria review

I'll open a short shared doc and drop a one-page checklist for procurement. Marissa — could you attach the peering playbook PDF and call out any common gotchas (route filters, edge NATs, etc.)? Ben — I'll loop you into procurement conversations if we need a short-term credit agreement.

Sam — do the dates above look reasonable from your end? If you prefer, we can compress the window and do tenant creation + ephemeral key on the same day.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — looping in the CS steps and a short checklist. We handle the peering coordination and can run a preflight call with your network engineer. Minimal artifacts we need from MedSync to open the peering request:
- AWS account ID (or GCP project number)
- Preferred VPC CIDR (example: 10.40.0.0/16) and confirmation it's non-overlapping
- Expected egress IP ranges for allowlist
- Desired peering window (we have engineers available Aug 31 and Sep 1)

Common gotchas:
- Overlapping CIDRs (we ask teams to choose a /16 that doesn't conflict with 10.0/8 internal ranges)
- Firewall rules blocking inbound health-checks from our peering IPs
- Missing route propagation for cross-account routes

I've attached the peering playbook (peer_playbook.pdf) with a step-by-step checklist and the template network manifest to paste into your ticket. I'll propose a 30-min preflight call — would Aug 26 at 10am PT work for your engineer?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
